dataPatches.reason: The first unit glyph remains visually unresolved. Preserve both 11′ × 1″ and 11″ × 1″; do not normalize a numeric area. Independent review does not resolve the glyph. Creature capacity remains a separate, readable effect rule.

The magic-user entry supplies its own 1″ × 1″ square/level header and explicitly follows the druid spell except as noted above. Its data does not import the druid dimensional examples. The stale inherited-area warning can be removed.

The explicit stopped-skill list is pick pockets, open locks, find traps, remove traps, plus read magic never gained. The following fifth-level freeze sentence refers to those ended skills. A separate paragraph says the acrobat retains movement/hiding/hearing/language abilities acquired through fifth level and explicitly continues climbing. It does not expressly say the four retained abilities remain frozen or cannot improve. Calling that an explicit resolution overstates the source. UA25 additionally says that in all other respects except as indicated the acrobat is treated as a thief, including followers and other special abilities. This general carryover rule is relevant and cannot be omitted when assessing progression.
dataPatches.recommendedNote: UA p.23 explicitly freezes pick pockets, opening locks, and finding/removing traps at fifth-level ability, and reading magical writings is never gained. It says the acrobat retains move silently, hide in shadows, hear noise, and read languages acquired through fifth level, while climb walls increases with experience level. UA p.25 generally treats the acrobat as a thief except as indicated. These passages do not expressly give a new progression for the four retained abilities; no categorical freeze or automatic increases are supplied here.
dataPatches.formalStatusDisposition: The source does not print two contradictory progression rules. A downgrade from formal source-conflict to a bounded unresolved interpretation is reasonable, but do not clear the uncertainty or supply an automatic progression/freeze. Preserve or reword the corresponding pendingMechanics caution.

dataPatches.reason: UA41 explicitly says a druid of indicated or lower level, and initiation is bestowed on a recipient beginning seventh level. However UA42 also gives a caster qualification: usually another druid of seventh or higher level performs initiation; unusual self-casting is allowed. The proposed caster/recipient-only explanation omits this continuation.
dataPatches.recommendedNote: UA p.41 prints that a druid of the indicated or lower level can cast each listed rite. Initiation is performed on a druid beginning seventh-level advancement; pp.41–42 say the recipient usually seeks another druid of seventh or higher level to perform it, with unusual self-casting allowed. Preserve the printed general wording and this rite-specific procedure.
dataPatches.formalStatusDisposition: The old claim based only on implied hierarchy may be retired after the note includes both pages. Treat the explicit initiation procedure as a specific qualifier; do not infer an unprinted universal minimum caster rank or claim all relevant thresholds concern recipients.

dataPatches.reason: Original pixels print pin or ivory or silver. Both omitted terms must be restored. Preserve the odd printed relation; do not silently normalize or to of or choose a pin material.

newFormalConflicts.reason: PHB19 summary prints class limit14. Its footnotes do not resolve the value. PHB30 specifically supplies the level15 Grandfather row and a challenge/assassination procedure for a fourteenth-level assassin. This is a conditional exception in the detailed class rules, not an unexplained choice between two alternative progressions. Preserve both printed locations, but do not present attaining15 as unresolved.
newFormalConflicts.allowedNote: PHB p.19 summarizes the assassin class limit as14; p.30 gives a conditional route to15 by defeating the Grandfather of Assassins, alongside its fifteenth-level advancement row.

newFormalConflicts.reason: UA ordinary-attack table visibly places paladin12 in both7–12 at3/2 rounds and12–18 at2/1round. PHB uses7–12 then13up. No table footnote selects one UA12 row. The ordinary table concerns thrusting/striking weapons and excludes the stated under-one-HD/normal-human melee case. Specialized fighter/ranger rates are separately excluded in UA.
newFormalConflicts.requiredQualification: Scope to this ordinary weapon-attack table and retain its explicit exclusions; do not assert one universal level12 attack rate. PHB-versus-UA progression is a printed variant; the internal UA overlap is the actual contradiction.

newFormalConflicts.reason: The table visibly includes seventh level in up to7th and7th–8th, with different age/duration/question allowances. No adjacent footnote resolves it. The range header also prints bare1. Preserve the missing unit as uncertainty; the overlap, rather than unit omission alone, supports source-conflict.

Header prints10″cube/level, prose says ten cubic inches per level, and the fourteenth-level examples7″×2″×1″ and1″×1″×14″ each give14cubic inches rather than140. The header/prose/example readings must remain separate; no numeric total should be supplied.

PHB hit-point benefit and double-hit-point death penalty occur in the paragraph beginning Normal familiars. The next paragraph explicitly delegates special-familiar powers to MM. Both MM imp and quasit entries print the special four-level death loss. The proposal removes the normal/special distinction and invents a stacking question.
